$comment: A line or two about Earth's rivers, lakes and seas, for the inspect window on one, as an English reader of 1790 might be told it: nothing after the first of January 1790. Each is filed under the name the world gives the thing and the ids of every piece of it world:names carries - a Wikidata id where the source gives one, otherwise its file, number and name - so that the four pieces of the Rhine say one thing and the two Dwinas, Riga's and Archangel's, each say their own. world:names gives every carried piece its line, beside the names the game server reads, and says how many it gave and which ids its world lacks. Written by an agent on 2026-10-07 for the rivers Natural Earth ranks 0 to 5 and those the review of 1790 named, the lakes it ranks 0 to 2 and the best known beyond, and the seas it ranks 0 to 3 and those the review named: a first draft, Adam's to correct. See decision record 0087.

rivers.name: Tongariro
rivers.about: It runs down from the burning mountains of the North Island of New Zealand into the great lake at its heart, country no European has seen; Cook charted only the coasts.

rivers.name: Irrawaddy Delta
rivers.about: The mouths of the river of Ava, braided through the rice country of Pegu to the Bay of Bengal. The Burmese kings have held Pegu since they took it from the Mons in 1757.

rivers.name: Ucayali
rivers.about: A great head of the Maragnon, running north through forests that Spanish friars have entered and left again, among the Conibo and the Shipibo.

rivers.name: Tuotuo
rivers.about: The farthest head of the Kiang, a braid of streams on the high cold plain of Tibet, which no European has followed.

rivers.name: Lena
rivers.about: The great river of eastern Siberia, which carries the Russians' boats from the portages down past Yakutsk to the Frozen Ocean; the furs of the north come up it.

rivers.name: Tongtian
rivers.about: The Kiang as it runs off the plateau of Tibet, the River Through Heaven to the Chinese, in the grazing country of the Tibetans and the Mongols of Koko Nor.

rivers.name: Mountain Nile
rivers.about: The Nile above the great swamps, the River of the Mountain to the Arabs, which no traveller from Egypt has followed to its head.

rivers.name: Mississippi
rivers.about: The great river of the middle of America, the western bound of the United States since the peace of 1783. Spain holds New Orleans and the west bank, and has shut the river's mouth to American boats since 1784.

rivers.name: Yangtze
rivers.about: The Kiang in the mountains of Yunnan and Sichuan, the River of Golden Sand, where men wash its gravels for gold before it turns east for China proper.

rivers.name: White Nile
rivers.about: The White Nile through the Sudd, a sea of reeds and floating islands where the river loses itself; the Shilluk and the Dinka live along it, and no European has been.

rivers.name: Bahr el Abiad
rivers.about: The White River of the Arabs, running north through the Funj kingdom of Sennar to meet the Blue. Where it comes from, nobody outside Africa knows.

rivers.name: Yang-tse-kiang
rivers.about: The great river of China, the Kiang, which divides the empire into north and south and carries the rice and salt of its provinces down to Nankin and the sea. The Jesuits mapped it for the Emperor Kang-hi.

rivers.name: Rosetta Branch
rivers.about: The western of the Nile's two mouths, reaching the sea at Rosetta, through which the grain and the rice of the Delta go round to Alexandria.

rivers.name: Damietta Branch
rivers.about: The eastern of the Nile's two mouths, where St Louis's crusade landed in 1249 and came to grief; Damietta at its end sends the Delta's rice to Syria.

rivers.name: Bykovskaya Protoka
rivers.about: The eastern channel of the Lena's delta, the one the river's boats take to the Frozen Ocean.

rivers.name: Olenekskaya Protoka
rivers.about: A western channel of the Lena's delta, reaching the Frozen Ocean through a maze of low islands.

rivers.name: Amazon
rivers.about: The greatest river in the world, which Orellana came down in 1542 and named for the women warriors he said he fought. The Portuguese hold it nearly to the Andes, and cacao comes down it to Pará.

rivers.name: Nile
rivers.about: The river of Egypt, whose summer flood is the whole of the country's wealth. The Mamluk beys rule it in the Porte's name, and where it comes from is still argued over.

rivers.name: Kiira
rivers.about: The Nile as it leaves the great lake of the Ganda, falling over rocks; nobody outside Africa knows that this is where the river comes from.

rivers.name: Kagera
rivers.about: The river that feeds the great lake from the west, out of the hills of Rwanda and Karagwe: the remotest of all the Nile's heads.

rivers.name: Madison
rivers.about: One of the three forks of the Missouri, high under the Shining Mountains, in the country of the Shoshone and the Blackfeet; no European is known to have reached it.

rivers.name: Missouri
rivers.about: The Missouri, which the Spanish traders of St Louis go up for the furs of the Osage and the Kansa. It comes muddy out of the west from nobody knows where.

rivers.name: Bahr el Jebel
rivers.about: The Nile coming north out of the lakes through the country of the Bari, all falls and rapids, which no traveller has reached from either end.

rivers.name: Oby
rivers.about: The Oby, one of the three great rivers of Siberia, running north past Surgut and Berezov to its long gulf in the Frozen Ocean. The Ostiaks fish it and pay the Empress their tribute in furs.

rivers.name: St. Lawrence
rivers.about: The river of Canada, the road from the sea to Quebec, Montreal and the Lakes. The British have held it since 1760, and the Montreal traders send their canoes from it to the far west for furs.

rivers.name: Danube
rivers.about: The great river of Europe, from the Black Forest past Vienna and Buda to the Black Sea. The Emperor and the Russians are at war with the Turks on its lower banks, and Belgrade fell to the Austrians in October.

rivers.name: Ideriyn
rivers.about: A head of the Selenga in the grasslands of the Khalkha Mongols, under the Manchu Emperor's rule since 1691.

rivers.name: Selinga
rivers.about: The Selenga, which flows out of Mongolia into Lake Baikal. At Kiachta near it Russian furs are bartered for Chinese tea, when Peking allows it: the trade has been shut since 1785.

rivers.name: Irtish
rivers.about: The Irtish, which comes out of the Chinese side of the Altai and runs north past Omsk and Tobolsk, the capital of Siberia, to the Oby. A line of Russian forts guards it against the Kazakhs.

rivers.name: Damqogkanbab
rivers.about: The head of the Sanpoo, rising near the holy lake of Manasarowar, where pilgrims from India walk round Mount Kailas.

rivers.name: Angara
rivers.about: The Angara, the one river that leaves Lake Baikal, running fast and clear past Irkutsk to the Yenisei. Irkutsk lives by the China trade.

rivers.name: Peace
rivers.about: The Peace River, named for a peace the Cree and the Beaver made at a point on it. The Montreal fur traders have lately come up it.

rivers.name: Mackenzie
rivers.about: The river Alexander Mackenzie followed to the Frozen Ocean last summer, hoping it led to the Pacific. It did not, and he calls it the River of Disappointment.

rivers.name: Za
rivers.about: The head of the Lan-tsang, the river the Laos call the Mekong, among the Tibetan herdsmen of Kham.

rivers.name: Paraná
rivers.about: The Paraná, which with the Paraguay and the Uruguay makes the River Plate. The Jesuits' mission towns stood along it until the King of Spain expelled them in 1767.

rivers.name: Lualaba
rivers.about: The Lualaba, rising in the copper country of Katanga and running north to nobody knows where; the Luba kings rule along it.

rivers.name: Slave
rivers.about: The Slave River, from the Lake of the Hills to the Slave Lake, through the country of the people the Cree call slaves: Mackenzie's road north.

rivers.name: Mekong
rivers.about: The Lan-tsang of Yunnan, which the Laos and the Cambodians downstream call the Mekong; it runs past the Tai princedoms of Sipsong Panna.

rivers.name: Zaire
rivers.about: The Zaire of the Portuguese, the river of Congo, whose mouth Diogo Cão found in 1482 and whose course nobody has followed above the falls.

rivers.name: Sanpoo
rivers.about: The Sanpoo, the river of Tibet, running east below Lhasa's valley. Whether it becomes the Burrampooter or the river of Ava, the Company's geographers argue.

rivers.name: Congo
rivers.about: The great river as it bends north and then west through the forest, unknown to anyone outside Africa; the Portuguese know only its mouth, and call it the Zaire.

rivers.name: Mecon
rivers.about: The Mecon, the river of Laos and Cambodia, which the Portuguese and the Dutch have sailed up as far as the falls. Cambodia, at its lower end, is pulled between Siam and Cochinchina.

rivers.name: Dihang
rivers.about: The Dihong, where the river of Tibet breaks through the mountains toward Assam, in the country of the Abor; nobody has followed it through.

rivers.name: Kilia Mouth
rivers.about: The northern mouth of the Danube, past Kilia and Ismail, the Turks' fortresses at the edge of their war with Russia.

rivers.name: St George's Mouth
rivers.about: The southern mouth of the Danube, reaching the sea through the reeds of the delta past the village of St George.

rivers.name: Sulina Mouth
rivers.about: The middle mouth of the Danube, where the ships of the Black Sea cross the bar at Sulina.

rivers.name: Burrampooter
rivers.about: The Burrampooter, which comes out of the mountains into Assam and joins the Ganges near the sea. Rennell first showed the Company how great a river it is.

rivers.name: Borcea
rivers.about: A side arm of the Danube in Wallachia, through the marshes below Silistria.

rivers.name: Oregon
rivers.about: The Oregon, the great river of the west that Carver wrote of, which no ship has yet entered: Heceta saw its bar in 1775, and Meares missed it in 1788.

rivers.name: Negro
rivers.about: The Rio Negro of Patagonia, where Spain built Carmen de Patagones at its mouth in 1779 to keep the British off the coast.

rivers.name: Negro
rivers.about: The Rio Negro, the black river that joins the Amazon at the Barra. Its upper waters reach the Orinoco by the Casiquiare, as the Jesuits said and La Condamine believed.

rivers.name: Negro
rivers.about: The Rio Negro of the Banda Oriental, through the cattle lands between Spanish Montevideo and the Portuguese frontier.

rivers.name: Grande
rivers.about: The Rio Grande, the head of the Paraná, on the edge of the gold country of Minas Gerais.

rivers.name: Grande
rivers.about: The Rio Grande of the Spanish lowlands below the Andes, running past Santa Cruz de la Sierra toward the Mamoré and the Amazon.

rivers.name: Yukon
rivers.about: A great river of the far north-west of America, known only to the peoples along it; the Russians of Kodiak have heard of it and no more.

rivers.name: Murray
rivers.about: A river of New Holland that no European knows of; the colony at Sydney Cove, two years old, has seen only the coast.

rivers.name: Ganges
rivers.about: The holy river of the Hindus, which pilgrims bathe in at Hurdwar where it leaves the mountains; the Company holds it from Benares to the sea.

rivers.name: Indus
rivers.about: The Indus, Alexander's river, which runs down from the Punjab of the Sikhs through Sind of the Talpur amirs to the sea at Tatta.

rivers.name: Niger
rivers.about: The Niger, which Europe argues runs east or west. It passes Timbuctoo, a city no Christian has seen in two hundred years, and the African Association in London has lately sent men to find it.

rivers.name: Ubangi
rivers.about: A great northern branch of the Zaire, in forests nobody from outside has entered.

rivers.name: Teslin
rivers.about: A head of the great north-western river, in the mountains the Tlingit traders cross to barter with the peoples inland.

rivers.name: Euphrates
rivers.about: The Euphrates of Eden and Babylon, which the Porte holds from Armenia to Bussorah; the caravans from Aleppo to Baghdad keep to the desert beside it.

rivers.name: Shiquan
rivers.about: The head of the Indus in western Tibet, the Lion River, near the holy mountain Kailas; the merchants of Ladakh carry its wool.

rivers.name: Hoang-ho
rivers.about: The Yellow River, China's Sorrow, whose floods and changes of course have drowned whole provinces; the Emperor keeps an army of men on its dykes.

rivers.name: Abay
rivers.about: The Abay, which James Bruce, a Scot, followed to its springs at Gish in 1770 and called the head of the Nile; it rises south of Lake Tzana and circles Gojjam.

rivers.name: Volga
rivers.about: The Volga, the greatest river of Europe, Russia's road from Tver past Kazan and Saratov to Astrakhan and the Caspian; its barges are hauled upstream by men.

rivers.name: Zambeze
rivers.about: The Zambeze, which the Portuguese go up from the coast as far as Zumbo for gold and ivory. Up here, in the floodplain of the Lozi, no European has been.

rivers.name: Shire
rivers.about: The Shire, running out of the Lake Maravi to the Zambeze; the Portuguese know of the lake from it, and from traders.

rivers.name: Amur
rivers.about: The Amur, the Black Dragon River of the Manchus, which the treaty of Nerchinsk gave to China in 1689 and closed to the Russians.

rivers.name: Blue Nile
rivers.about: The Blue Nile, running down from Abyssinia through Sennar of the Funj kings; its summer flood is the flood of Egypt.

rivers.name: Hailar
rivers.about: A head of the Argun on the plains of the Barga Mongols, where the Manchu Emperor's bannermen keep the Russian frontier.

rivers.name: Orinoco
rivers.about: The Orinoco, the river of Guiana, where Raleigh sought El Dorado. The Spanish hold Angostura on it, and its falls at Atures stop every boat.

rivers.name: Weir
rivers.about: A river of New Holland's interior, unknown to the new colony at Sydney Cove.

rivers.name: Kibali
rivers.about: A head of the Uele in the far north-east of the Congo forest, unknown beyond it.

rivers.name: Allegany
rivers.about: The Allegany, which joins the Monongahela at Pittsburgh to make the Ohio; settlers have been pushing up it since the Iroquois sold their lands at Fort Stanwix.

rivers.name: Kasai
rivers.about: The Kasai, a great southern branch of the Zaire, among the Lunda and the Kuba, whose kings sell slaves and ivory to the Portuguese of Angola.

rivers.name: Barwon
rivers.about: A river of New Holland's interior that no European has seen.

rivers.name: Uele
rivers.about: A river of the northern Congo forest and of the Azande, unknown beyond it.

rivers.name: Ergun
rivers.about: The Argun, the frontier between the Russian and the Chinese empires since Nerchinsk; Cossacks and bannermen watch each other across it.

rivers.name: Darling
rivers.about: A river of New Holland's interior that no European knows.

rivers.name: Mamoré
rivers.about: The Mamoré, where the Jesuits gathered the Moxos into missions until 1767; it runs north to the Madeira and the Portuguese frontier.

rivers.name: Niagara
rivers.about: The Niagara, between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario, with its great falls. The British still hold Fort Niagara at its mouth, though the peace of 1783 gave it to the United States.

rivers.name: St. Clair
rivers.about: The St Clair, the strait from Lake Huron down to the little lake of St Clair and Detroit, which the British also keep.

rivers.name: Guaporé
rivers.about: The Guaporé, the frontier between Portuguese Mato Grosso and Spanish Moxos, where the Portuguese have built the fort of the Prince of Beira.

rivers.name: Madeira
rivers.about: The Madeira, named for the timber it carries, the Portuguese road from the Amazon up past dangerous rapids to the gold of Mato Grosso.

rivers.name: Ohio
rivers.about: The Ohio, La Belle Rivière of the French, the road west for Americans: settlers' flatboats come down it every spring, and Marietta was founded on it in 1788.

rivers.name: Shatt al Arab
rivers.about: The Tigris and the Euphrates joined below Corna, running past Bussorah to the Gulf; the Company keeps a factory at Bussorah.

rivers.name: Araguaia
rivers.about: The Araguaia, running north through Goiás to the Tocantins round the great island of Bananal; the Portuguese go up it after gold and Indians to settle.

rivers.name: Vaal
rivers.about: The Vaal, a branch of the Orange, on the high grasslands beyond the Cape Colony's border, among the Tswana and the Kora.

rivers.name: Aldan
rivers.about: The Aldan, part of the road from Yakutsk toward Okhotsk and the Pacific, up which the Russians drag their goods by river and by packhorse.

rivers.name: Snake
rivers.about: A great southern branch of the Oregon, in the country of the Shoshone; no European has been.

rivers.name: São Francisco
rivers.about: The river of the cattle country, running north through the backlands of Brazil: the road between the gold mines of Minas and the sugar coast of Bahia.

rivers.name: Rhine
rivers.about: The Rhine, out of the Alps past Basle, Strasburg, Mentz and Cologne to Holland, where it loses itself in many arms; a dozen princes take toll on it.

rivers.name: Sukhona
rivers.about: The Sukhona, which joins the Yug at Great Ustiug to make the Northern Dwina: the road of Russian trade to Archangel.

rivers.name: Shishhid Gol
rivers.about: A head of the Yenisei in the Darkhad valley of Mongolia, at the edge of the Manchu Emperor's lands.

rivers.name: Paranaíba
rivers.about: The Paranaíba, a head of the Paraná, between the gold districts of Goiás and Minas Gerais.

rivers.name: La Grande
rivers.about: The Great River of the East Main, running west to James Bay through country the Cree hunt for the Hudson's Bay Company's posts.

rivers.name: Rio del Norte
rivers.about: The River of the North, Spain's road up from Chihuahua to Santa Fe in New Mexico; El Paso stands on it.

rivers.name: Ural
rivers.about: The Ural, the Yaik until the Empress renamed it in 1775 to forget Pugachev, whose rising began among its Cossacks.

rivers.name: Saskatchewan
rivers.about: The Saskatchewan, the fur traders' river across the plains; Cumberland House of the Hudson's Bay Company stands near its lower end.

rivers.name: Yenisey
rivers.about: The Yenisei, the greatest of the Siberian rivers, running north past Krasnoyarsk and Yeniseisk to the Frozen Ocean.

rivers.name: Yssel
rivers.about: The Yssel, the arm of the Rhine that runs north past Zutphen and Deventer to the Zuyder Zee.

rivers.name: Tocantins
rivers.about: The Tocantins, which reaches the sea beside the Amazon's mouth below Belém of Pará; the Portuguese go up it to the gold of Goiás.

rivers.name: Dnieper
rivers.about: The Dnieper, the Borysthenes of the Greeks and Kiev's river, between Poland and Russia above Kiev and Russian below it to Kherson at its mouth; its rapids stop boats below Ekaterinoslav.

rivers.name: North Saskatchewan
rivers.about: The North Saskatchewan, up which the Montreal traders and the Hudson's Bay men race each other to build posts among the Blackfoot and the Cree.

rivers.name: Bafing
rivers.about: The Bafing, the black river, head of the Senegal, in the Fouta Djallon highlands of the Fula almamys.

rivers.name: Bénoué
rivers.about: The Benue, a great eastern river of Africa whose waters some think are the Niger's; no European knows it.

rivers.name: Tigris
rivers.about: The Tigris, the swift river, past Mosul and Baghdad, where the pasha rules nearly in his own right.

rivers.name: Petchora
rivers.about: The Petchora, in the far north-east of Russia, where the Samoyeds herd reindeer and the Old Believers have hidden from the Church.

rivers.name: Indaiá
rivers.about: A head of the São Francisco in Minas Gerais, where gold and diamonds have drawn men inland.

rivers.name: Kovyma
rivers.about: The Kolyma, at the far end of Siberia, where the Russians of Nizhnekolymsk trade with the Chukchi; the Frozen Ocean is at its mouth.

rivers.name: Nmai
rivers.about: A head of the river of Ava, in the hills of the Kachin, unknown to Europeans.

rivers.name: Magdalena
rivers.about: The Magdalena, the road from Cartagena up to Santa Fe de Bogotá, capital of New Granada; its boats are poled for weeks against the current.

rivers.name: Neuquén
rivers.about: A river of the Pehuenche country east of the Andes, beyond Spain's frontier.

rivers.name: Nanpan
rivers.about: A head of the West River in the hills of Yunnan, among the Yi and the Zhuang.

rivers.name: Seine
rivers.about: The Seine, the river of Paris, where the Bastille fell last July and the King now lives under the people's eye.

rivers.name: Oder
rivers.about: The Oder, Prussia's river, past Breslau and Frankfort to Stettin and the Baltic.

rivers.name: Arkansaw
rivers.about: The Arkansaw, coming out of the plains to the Mississippi, where the Spanish keep Arkansas Post among the Quapaw.

rivers.name: Senegal
rivers.about: The Senegal, France's river in Africa: Saint-Louis stands on an island at its mouth, and gum and slaves come down it.

rivers.name: Kyzyl-Khem
rivers.about: A head of the Yenisei in the Uriankhai country, where the Manchu Emperor's Mongols and the Russians both claim tribute.

rivers.name: Salween
rivers.about: The Salween, which runs down from Tibet through gorges nobody passes and out to the sea at Martaban.

rivers.name: Dwina
rivers.about: The Dwina of Archangel, Russia's old way to the sea before Petersburg: the English came to trade on it in Queen Elizabeth's day, and timber and hemp still go out by it.

rivers.name: Dwina
rivers.about: The Düna, the Dwina of Riga, which brings the hemp and the flax of Poland and White Russia down to Riga's merchants.

rivers.name: Benue
rivers.about: The Benue, a great eastern river of Africa whose waters some think are the Niger's; no European knows it.

rivers.name: Irrawaddy
rivers.about: The river of Ava, which the Burmese kings rule from Amarapura; its teak and rubies go down to the sea.

rivers.name: Leck
rivers.about: The Leck, the arm of the Rhine that runs west past the province of Utrecht to Rotterdam's waters.

rivers.name: Shatt al Hai
rivers.about: A channel between the Tigris and the Euphrates, in the marshes of the Muntafiq Arabs.

rivers.name: Malyy Yenisey
rivers.about: The Little Yenisei, in the Uriankhai country under the Sayan mountains.

rivers.name: Verkhniy Yenisey
rivers.about: The upper Yenisei, breaking out of the Sayan mountains into Russian Siberia.

rivers.name: Nu
rivers.about: The Salween in Yunnan, the Angry River to the Chinese, deep in its gorge.

rivers.name: Hongshui
rivers.about: The Red Water River of Guangxi, among the Zhuang.

rivers.name: Quan
rivers.about: A stretch of the West River's waters in Guangxi, among the Zhuang.

rivers.name: Xun
rivers.about: The West River in Guangxi, carrying the province's rice and timber down to Canton.

rivers.name: Waal
rivers.about: The Waal, the Rhine's broadest arm, past Nimeguen to the Maese.

rivers.name: Braco Menor
rivers.about: The lesser arm of the Araguaia, round the great island of Bananal.

rivers.name: Nelson
rivers.about: The Nelson, which carries Lake Winnipeg's water to Hudson's Bay at York Factory, where the Company's ships call once a year.

rivers.name: Si-kiang
rivers.about: The West River, which comes down to Canton, the one port where Europeans may trade with China.

rivers.name: Orange
rivers.about: The Orange River, which Colonel Gordon named in 1779 for the Prince of Orange: the northern edge of the Cape Colony's world.

rivers.name: Ebro
rivers.about: The Ebro, the river that named Iberia, past Saragossa to the sea below Tortosa; the Imperial Canal of Aragon runs beside it.

rivers.name: Stikine
rivers.about: A river of the north-west coast, where the Tlingit trade with the peoples inland; the ships that come for sea-otter skins know only its mouth.

rivers.name: San Juan
rivers.about: The San Juan, the outlet of the Lake of Nicaragua to the Caribbean, which the British tried to take in 1780 to cut Spain's empire in two.

rivers.name: Elbe
rivers.about: The Elbe, out of Bohemia past Dresden and Magdeburg to Hamburg and the German Ocean.

rivers.name: Thelon
rivers.about: A river of the Barren Grounds, where the Chipewyan follow the caribou and no trader goes.

rivers.name: Colorado
rivers.about: The Colorado, the red river, whose great canyon Spaniards saw in 1540 and Father Garcés crossed in 1776.

rivers.name: Colorado
rivers.about: The Colorado of Patagonia, the frontier of the Pampas between Spain's Buenos Aires and the free Indians.

rivers.name: Tagus
rivers.about: The Tagus, which rises in Spain and reaches the sea at Lisbon, whose harbour is the finest in Europe; the city has been rebuilt since the earthquake of 1755.

rivers.name: Vistula
rivers.about: Poland's great river, which carries the grain of the Polish plains past Warsaw to Dantzic, whence it is shipped to Amsterdam. Prussia holds its lower banks and takes toll on the trade.

rivers.name: Sacramento
rivers.about: A river of the great valley of California, which the Spanish of San Francisco have looked at and not settled.

rivers.name: Neva
rivers.about: The Neva, short and deep, from Lake Ladoga to the Gulf of Finland; Petersburg, Peter's capital, stands at its mouth.

rivers.name: Cherokee River
rivers.about: The Cherokee River, the Tennessee, through the lands of the Cherokee and the Chickamauga, where Carolina's settlers are pressing in.

rivers.name: Jaxartes
rivers.about: The Jaxartes, the Sihon of the Arabs, which Alexander made his frontier; the Kazakhs and the khans of Kokand graze and fight along it to the Sea of Aral.

rivers.name: Naryn
rivers.about: The Naryn, the head of the Jaxartes, in the mountains of the Kirghiz.

rivers.name: Klamath
rivers.about: A river of the coast north of Spanish California, of the Karuk and the Yurok; no European has been up it.

rivers.name: Athabasca
rivers.about: The Athabasca, where Peter Pond built his post in 1778, the first beyond the height of land; it runs to the Lake of the Hills and Fort Chipewyan.

rivers.name: Svir
rivers.about: The Svir, which carries Lake Onega's water to Ladoga: part of the waterway that feeds Petersburg.

rivers.name: Black Volta
rivers.about: A branch of the Volta north of the Ashanti's power, in the country of the Lobi and the Dagara.

rivers.name: Volta
rivers.about: The Volta, which reaches the Gold Coast at Ada; the Ashanti's power reaches over its middle course.

rivers.name: Culuene
rivers.about: A head of the Xingu in the heart of Brazil, where no Portuguese has been.

rivers.name: Godavery
rivers.about: The Godavery, the Ganges of the south to the Hindus, running across the Deccan through the Nizam's country to the Company's coast.

rivers.name: Tobol
rivers.about: The Tobol, which meets the Irtish at Tobolsk, the capital of Siberia, named for it.

rivers.name: Nizhnyaya Tunguska
rivers.about: The Lower Tunguska, which the Evenks hunt along, running to the Yenisei through forest that has no towns.

rivers.name: Maragnon
rivers.about: The Maragnon, which Spain calls the Amazon's true head, rushing out of the Andes through its gorges to the forest.

rivers.name: Caquetá
rivers.about: The Caquetá, the Japurá of the Portuguese, between the claims of Spain and Portugal.

rivers.name: Holston
rivers.about: The Holston, where the first settlers over the mountains made the State of Franklin, which Congress would not have.

rivers.name: Pamir
rivers.about: The Pamir, on the Roof of the World, where Marco Polo's road crossed toward China.

rivers.name: Fraser
rivers.about: A river of the far west of America, unknown to any European; the Dakelh fish its salmon.

rivers.name: Indigirka
rivers.about: A river of north-east Siberia, of the Yukaghirs and a few Russian traders.

rivers.name: Sprague
rivers.about: A river of the high desert of the Klamath people, unknown to Europeans.

rivers.name: Juruena
rivers.about: A head of the Tapajós in Mato Grosso, where Portuguese prospectors look for gold.

rivers.name: Vychegda
rivers.about: The Vychegda, a river of the Russian north, which joins the Dwina below Great Ustiug.

rivers.name: Chixoy
rivers.about: A river of the highlands of Guatemala, running down to the Usumacinta.

rivers.name: Bío-Bío
rivers.about: The Biobío, Spain's frontier in Chile against the unconquered Araucanians.

rivers.name: Panj
rivers.about: The Panj, the head of the Oxus, through the mountain princedoms of Badakhshan.

rivers.name: Santa Cruz
rivers.about: A river of Patagonia, whose mouth Magellan's men found in 1520.

rivers.name: Xingu
rivers.about: The Xingu, a great southern branch of the Amazon, whose upper course no Portuguese knows.

rivers.name: Oxus
rivers.about: The Oxus, the Jihon, the old boundary between Iran and Turan, flowing past Khiva's country to the Sea of Aral.

rivers.name: Tapajós
rivers.about: The Tapajós, clear-watered, joining the Amazon at Santarém.

rivers.name: Trofimovskaya Protoka
rivers.about: A channel of the Lena's delta on the Frozen Ocean.

rivers.name: Tumatskaya Protoka
rivers.about: A channel of the Lena's delta on the Frozen Ocean.

rivers.name: Japurá
rivers.about: The Japurá, the Caquetá of the Spaniards, joining the Amazon.

rivers.name: Loire
rivers.about: The Loire, the longest river of France, past Orleans and Tours to Nantes, whose merchants grew rich on sugar and slaves.

rivers.name: Copper-mine River
rivers.about: The river Samuel Hearne reached in 1771 and followed to the Frozen Ocean. He found little copper, and saw his Chipewyan guides kill the Inuit at the falls.

rivers.name: Rio Grande de Santiago
rivers.about: The river of New Galicia, which falls from Lake Chapala past Guadalajara's country to the Pacific.

rivers.name: Purificacion
rivers.about: A river of New Santander, on Spain's north-eastern frontier in Mexico.

rivers.name: Panuco
rivers.about: The Pánuco, which reaches the Gulf of Mexico at Tampico.

rivers.name: St. Pierre
rivers.about: The St Pierre of the French traders, down which the Sioux come to trade where it meets the Mississippi.

rivers.name: Ouisconsin
rivers.about: The Ouisconsin, by which Marquette and Joliet came to the Mississippi in 1673: the fur road from Green Bay to the Prairie du Chien.

rivers.name: Tombeckbee
rivers.about: The Tombeckbee, of the Choctaw and the Chickasaw, which Spain watches from Mobile.

rivers.name: Rio Grande de Matagalpa
rivers.about: A river of the Mosquito Shore, which the British gave up to Spain by the convention of 1786.

rivers.name: Kentucke
rivers.about: The Kentucke, of the hunting ground Boone opened. Virginia's settlers have crowded in since the war, and they want a state of their own.

rivers.name: Chirripó del Atlántico
rivers.about: A river of the mountains of Costa Rica, running down to the Caribbean coast.

rivers.name: Alatamaha
rivers.about: The Alatamaha of Georgia, among live oaks and rice swamps, long the bound between Georgia's settlers and the Creeks.

rivers.name: Great Kanhawa
rivers.about: The Great Kanhawa, where the Virginians beat the Shawnee at Point Pleasant in 1774.

rivers.name: Santa María
rivers.about: A river of the isthmus of Panama, running to the Pacific.

rivers.name: Great Pedee
rivers.about: The Great Pedee of the Carolinas, where Marion's men hid in the swamps in the late war.

rivers.name: South Branch of Patowmack
rivers.about: The South Branch, through the valleys of Virginia, where Washington surveyed land as a young man.

rivers.name: Ottawa
rivers.about: The Grand River of the Ottawas, the canoe road of the fur trade from Montreal to the Lakes and the west.

rivers.name: Patowmack
rivers.about: The Patowmack, Washington's river, past Mount Vernon; the President's company is cutting a canal round its falls.

rivers.name: West Branch of Susquehannah
rivers.about: The West Branch, Pennsylvania's frontier, where the Fair Play men lived beyond the law.

rivers.name: Great Whale River
rivers.about: A river of the East Main, where the Company has hunted the white whale.

rivers.name: Susquehannah
rivers.about: The Susquehannah, the long river of Pennsylvania, running to Chesapeake Bay; its upper valley was the Iroquois' until Sullivan burned their towns in 1779.

rivers.name: Hudson's River
rivers.about: Hudson's River, the road from New York to Albany and Canada, where General Burgoyne surrendered at Saratoga in 1777.

rivers.name: Sorel
rivers.about: The Sorel, the old war road from Lake Champlain down to the St Lawrence.

rivers.name: St. Maurice
rivers.about: The St Maurice, which meets the St Lawrence at Three Rivers, where Canada's first iron forges stand.

rivers.name: Rivière aux Mélèzes
rivers.about: The river of larches, in the north of the interior of Labrador.

rivers.name: Essequebo
rivers.about: The Essequebo, the river of the Dutch colony in Guiana, of sugar estates worked by slaves.

rivers.name: Surinam
rivers.about: The river of Surinam, where the Dutch town of Paramaribo stands; the colony's slaves run off to the Maroons of the forest.

rivers.name: Gambia
rivers.about: The Gambia, England's river in Africa, which traders go up for slaves, wax and ivory.

rivers.name: Sierra Leone River
rivers.about: The river of Sierra Leone, where London's philanthropists landed freed black settlers in 1787.

rivers.name: Minho
rivers.about: The Minho, the border between Portugal and Spanish Galicia.

rivers.name: Douro
rivers.about: The Douro, which brings the port wine down from the upper valley to Oporto, whose English merchants ship it.

rivers.name: Pisuerga
rivers.about: A river of Old Castile, past Valladolid.

rivers.name: Záncara
rivers.about: A river of La Mancha, dry for much of the summer.

rivers.name: Guadalaviar
rivers.about: The Guadalaviar, which waters the orchards of Valencia.

rivers.name: Xucar
rivers.about: The Xucar, which waters the rice fields of the coast of Valencia.

rivers.name: Thames
rivers.about: The river of London, the busiest port in the world, whose Pool below the bridge is a forest of masts.

rivers.name: Garonne
rivers.about: The Garonne, which brings the wines of Guyenne down to Bourdeaux.

rivers.name: Scheld
rivers.about: The Scheld, the river of Antwerp, closed to shipping by the Dutch since 1648; the Emperor nearly went to war over it in 1784.

rivers.name: Saone
rivers.about: The Saône, slow and broad, which joins the Rhone at Lyons.

rivers.name: Meuse
rivers.about: The Meuse, out of Lorraine past Verdun and Sedan.

rivers.name: Maese
rivers.about: The Maese, which comes down past Liège and Maestricht to meet the Rhine's waters in Holland.

rivers.name: Rhone
rivers.about: The Rhone, which leaves the Lake of Geneva and runs fast past Lyons to the Mediterranean, the hardest river in France to go up.

rivers.name: Moselle
rivers.about: The Moselle, between vineyards from Lorraine to Coblentz, where it meets the Rhine.

rivers.name: Weser
rivers.about: The Weser, Bremen's river, through Hanover, which is King George's.

rivers.name: Po
rivers.about: The Po, across the plain of Lombardy from Piedmont to the Venetians' marshes; its floods are feared.

rivers.name: Mayne
rivers.about: The Mayne, which meets the Rhine at Mentz, past Frankfort, the city of the fairs and of the Emperors' crownings.

rivers.name: Glommen
rivers.about: The Glommen, Norway's greatest river, which floats the timber of the forests down to the sawmills at its mouth.

rivers.name: Gotha
rivers.about: The Gotha, which carries Lake Wener's water past the falls of Trollhätta to Gothenburg; a canal round the falls was begun and abandoned.

rivers.name: Tiber
rivers.about: The Tiber of Rome, yellow and slow, under the Pope's bridges.

rivers.name: Eger
rivers.about: The Eger of Bohemia, past the fortress the Emperor has built and named for his mother.

rivers.name: Klarälven
rivers.about: The Klar, which brings Wermeland's iron and timber down to Lake Wener at Carlstad.

rivers.name: Moldau
rivers.about: The Moldau, the river of Prague, under its old stone bridge.

rivers.name: Neisse
rivers.about: The Neisse of Lusatia, running down to the Oder.

rivers.name: Drave
rivers.about: The Drave, between Hungary and Croatia, joining the Danube below Esseck.

rivers.name: Kulpa
rivers.about: The Kulpa, at the edge of Croatia's military frontier.

rivers.name: Bober
rivers.about: A river of the mountains of Silesia.

rivers.name: Motala ström
rivers.about: The Motala, which carries Lake Wetter's water to the Baltic past the mills of Norrköping.

rivers.name: Dal
rivers.about: The Dal, of Dalecarlia, whose men rose for Gustavus Vasa; the copper of Falun goes down to it.

rivers.name: Muhr
rivers.about: The Muhr, past Gratz, the capital of Styria.

rivers.name: Coanza
rivers.about: The Coanza of Angola, the Portuguese road inland from Loanda for slaves.

rivers.name: Raab
rivers.about: The Raab, where the Emperor's army beat the Turks at St Gotthard in 1664.

rivers.name: Glatz Neisse
rivers.about: The Neisse of Glatz, through the county Prussia took from the Empress Maria Theresa.

rivers.name: Ångermanälven
rivers.about: A river of Swedish Norrland, of timber and salmon.

rivers.name: Netze
rivers.about: The Netze, which Prussia joined to the Vistula by the Bromberg canal in 1774.

rivers.name: Narenta
rivers.about: The Narenta of Herzegovina, under the Turks' old bridge at Mostar.

rivers.name: March
rivers.about: The March, between Hungary and Austria, on whose field King Ottokar fell in 1278.

rivers.name: Save
rivers.about: The Save, the frontier between the Emperor's Croatia and the Turks' Bosnia, which meets the Danube at Belgrade.

rivers.name: Save
rivers.about: The Sabi, which the Portuguese of Sofala know as the road to the old gold lands of Monomotapa.

rivers.name: Waag
rivers.about: The Waag, the longest river of Upper Hungary.

rivers.name: Skellefteälven
rivers.about: A river of Swedish Lapland, of the Lapps' reindeer and of salmon.

rivers.name: Stora Lule älv
rivers.about: A river of Swedish Lapland, falling through the mountains to the Gulf of Bothnia.

rivers.name: Theiss
rivers.about: The Theiss, the great river of the Hungarian plain, slow, marshy and full of fish.

rivers.name: Alle
rivers.about: The Alle of East Prussia, running north to the Pregel.

rivers.name: Temes
rivers.about: The Temes of the Banat, which the Emperor took from the Turks in 1718 and has settled with Swabians.

rivers.name: Windau
rivers.about: The Windau of Courland, whose duke is the Empress's man.

rivers.name: Lule älv
rivers.about: A river of Swedish Lapland, reaching the Gulf of Bothnia at Luleå.

rivers.name: Niemen
rivers.about: The Niemen, which carries the timber and grain of Lithuania down to Memel; the Teutonic Knights' castles stand along it.

rivers.name: Kumo
rivers.about: The Kumo of Swedish Finland, past Biörneborg to the sea.

rivers.name: Sebes Körös
rivers.about: A river of the Hungarian plain under the mountains of Transylvania.

rivers.name: Strymon
rivers.about: The Strymon, the river of Amphipolis, under the Turks in Macedonia.

rivers.name: Maros
rivers.about: The Maros, which carries the salt of Transylvania down to the Theiss.

rivers.name: Bug
rivers.about: The Bug, between the provinces of Poland, joining the Narew on its way to the Vistula.

rivers.name: Tornea
rivers.about: The Tornea, where Maupertuis measured a degree of the meridian in 1736 to prove the earth flattened at the poles.

rivers.name: Aluta
rivers.about: The Aluta, which breaks through the Carpathians at the Red Tower pass into Wallachia.

rivers.name: Szamos
rivers.about: A river of northern Transylvania.

rivers.name: Pernau
rivers.about: The Pernau of Livonia, Russian since Peter's wars.

rivers.name: Kymmene
rivers.about: The Kymmene, the frontier between Swedish and Russian Finland since 1743.

rivers.name: Wilia
rivers.about: The Wilia, the river of Wilna, the capital of Lithuania.

rivers.name: Aa
rivers.about: The Aa of Livonia, through the woods to the Gulf of Riga.

rivers.name: Embach
rivers.about: The Embach, the river of Dorpat.

rivers.name: Maritza
rivers.about: The Maritza, the Hebrus of the Greeks, past Philippopolis and Adrianople.

rivers.name: Ulea
rivers.about: The Ulea of Swedish Finland, down which the tar of Kajana comes to Uleåborg.

rivers.name: Sereth
rivers.about: The Sereth of Moldavia, where the Russians and Austrians beat the Turks at Fokshani and on the Rymnik in the summer and autumn just past.

rivers.name: Dniester
rivers.about: The Dniester, the frontier between Poland and the Turks, where the Russians took Bender in November.

rivers.name: Pruth
rivers.about: The Pruth of Moldavia, where Peter the Great was trapped by the Turks in 1711.

rivers.name: Hermus
rivers.about: The Hermus of Lydia, whose valley sends figs and raisins to Smyrna.

rivers.name: Cayster
rivers.about: The Cayster, the river of Ephesus, which silted up the harbour until the city died.

rivers.name: Kemi
rivers.about: The Kemi of Swedish Lapland, a salmon river reaching the Gulf of Bothnia.

rivers.name: Meander
rivers.about: The Meander, which wanders so much that it gave its name to every winding.

rivers.name: Pripet
rivers.about: The Pripet, through the great marshes of Polesie.

rivers.name: Bog
rivers.about: The Bog, the Hypanis, which reaches the Black Sea at Oczakow, taken by the Russians in 1788.

rivers.name: Kizil Irmak
rivers.about: The Red River of Anatolia, the Halys, which Croesus crossed to lose his kingdom.

rivers.name: Jordan
rivers.about: The Jordan, where Christ was baptised; pilgrims come down from Jerusalem at Easter to bathe in it.

rivers.name: Donetz
rivers.about: The Donetz, of the Don Cossacks and the settlers of Slobodsk Ukraine.

rivers.name: Tacazze
rivers.about: The Tacazze of Abyssinia, which runs to the Nile; Bruce crossed it on his road to Gondar.

rivers.name: Don
rivers.about: The Don, the Tanais, of the Don Cossacks, which reaches the Sea of Azoph.

rivers.name: Cuban
rivers.about: The Cuban, Russia's new frontier against the Circassians since the Crimea was taken.

rivers.name: Araxes
rivers.about: The Araxes of Armenia, under Ararat, running east to the Kur.

rivers.name: Kur
rivers.about: The Kur, the Cyrus, past Tiflis, the Georgian king's capital, to the Caspian.

rivers.name: Behut
rivers.about: The Behut, the Hydaspes, where Alexander beat Porus.

rivers.name: Rauvee
rivers.about: The Rauvee, the river of Lahore, in the country of the Sikhs.

rivers.name: Chenaub
rivers.about: The Chenaub of the Punjab, the Acesines of Alexander's historians.

rivers.name: Tapty
rivers.about: The Tapty, which reaches the sea at Surat, where the English began their trade in India.

rivers.name: Kistna
rivers.about: The Kistna, whose diamond mines near Golconda gave the world the Koh-i-Noor.

rivers.name: Toombuddra
rivers.about: The Toombuddra, which runs past the ruins of Vijayanagar.

rivers.name: Ili
rivers.about: The Ili, where the Manchu Emperor's armies destroyed the Zunghars in 1757 and planted a garrison at Kuldja.

rivers.name: Beyah
rivers.about: The Beyah, the Hyphasis, where Alexander's army refused to march any further.

rivers.name: Cavery
rivers.about: The Cavery, which runs past Seringapatam, Tippoo Sultan's island capital, and waters the rice of Tanjore.

rivers.name: Chumbul
rivers.about: The Chumbul, through the ravines of the Rajputs and the Marathas' Gwalior.

rivers.name: Nerbudda
rivers.about: The Nerbudda, holy to the Hindus, the boundary between Hindostan and the Deccan.

rivers.name: Jumna
rivers.about: The Jumna, past Delhi, where the Mughal emperor, blinded by Ghulam Kadir in 1788, now rules by the Maratha Scindia's leave, and on down to Agra and its Taj.

rivers.name: Setlege
rivers.about: The Setlege, the eastern edge of the Sikhs' Punjab.

rivers.name: Coleroon
rivers.about: The Coleroon, the northern arm of the Cavery's delta in the Carnatic.

rivers.name: Gogra
rivers.about: The Gogra, through Oude, whose Nawab rules under the Company's protection.

rivers.name: Soane
rivers.about: The Soane, which meets the Ganges near Patna.

rivers.name: Gunduck
rivers.about: The Gunduck, out of Nepal, whose Gorkha kings have lately conquered the hills.

rivers.name: Mahanuddy
rivers.about: The Mahanuddy, the river of Cuttack in Orissa, which the Marathas hold.

rivers.name: Tom
rivers.about: The Tom, past Tomsk, a Siberian town on the fur road.

rivers.name: Coosy
rivers.about: The Coosy, the sorrow of Bihar, which changes its bed and drowns the land.

rivers.name: Teesta
rivers.about: The Teesta, out of Sikkim, which broke into a new bed in the great flood of 1787.

rivers.name: Menam
rivers.about: The Menam, the mother of waters, on which Bangkok, Siam's new capital, stands.

rivers.name: Martuwarra
rivers.about: A great river of northern New Holland, unknown to Europeans.

rivers.name: Songari
rivers.about: The Songari of Manchuria, the homeland the Manchu emperors keep closed to Chinese settlers.

rivers.name: Kamtschatka
rivers.about: The river of Kamtschatka, where Bering built his ship in 1728.

rivers.name: Anadir
rivers.about: The Anadir, of the Chukchi, where the Russians have given up their fort.

rivers.name: Māwheranui
rivers.about: A river of the western coast of New Zealand, where the Māori find greenstone.

rivers.name: Kawatiri
rivers.about: A river of the western coast of New Zealand, unknown to Europeans.

rivers.name: Te Awakairangi
rivers.about: A river at the harbour Cook saw but did not enter, at the south of New Zealand's northern island.

lakes.name: Great Bear Lake
lakes.about: A great lake of the far north-west, which Mackenzie heard of from the Dene as he went down to the Frozen Ocean last summer; no European has seen it.

lakes.name: Slave Lake
lakes.about: The Slave Lake, which Mackenzie crossed last summer on his way to the Frozen Ocean; the North West Company's men trade on its shores.

lakes.name: McLeod Bay
lakes.about: The eastern arm of the Slave Lake, deep under cliffs, which Samuel Hearne crossed on the ice on his way home from the Copper-mine River.

lakes.name: Lake Winnipeg
lakes.about: Lake Winnipeg, the muddy water of the Cree: the crossroads of the fur trade between Hudson's Bay, the Saskatchewan and the Red River.

lakes.name: Lake Erie
lakes.about: The shallowest of the Great Lakes, named for the Erie nation the Iroquois destroyed; Connecticut has reserved its southern shore for settlers, and the Indians there dispute it.

lakes.name: Lake Ontario
lakes.about: The lowest of the Great Lakes, between Kingston and Niagara. The King's ships keep it, and the Loyalists who left the United States farm its northern shore.

lakes.name: Lake Saint Clair
lakes.about: The little lake between Huron and Erie, named by La Salle's men on St Clare's day in 1679; Detroit is just below it.

lakes.name: Lake Superior
lakes.about: The greatest lake in the world, the Lac Supérieur of the French; the canoes of the North West Company cross it every summer to the Grand Portage.

lakes.name: Lake Michigan
lakes.about: Lake Michigan, the great water of the Ottawa and the Potawatomi, with Michilimackinac at its strait, which the British hold.

lakes.name: Lake Huron
lakes.about: Lake Huron, the Mer Douce of Champlain, named for the Wendat whom the French called Hurons.

lakes.name: Lake Ladoga
lakes.about: The largest lake in Europe, whose storms drove Peter to dig a canal along its southern shore for the barges bound for Petersburg.

lakes.name: Lake Balkhash
lakes.about: A long lake of the Kazakh steppe, half fresh and half salt, at the edge of the Manchu Emperor's Ili country.

lakes.name: Lake Baikal
lakes.about: The Holy Sea of Siberia, the deepest water anyone knows, which the Russians cross by boat and on the ice on the road to Kiachta and China.

lakes.name: Mwitanzige
lakes.about: The lake of the kingdom of Bunyoro; nobody outside Africa knows that the Nile passes through it.

lakes.name: Lake Maravi
lakes.about: The lake of the Maravi, which the Portuguese know by report; the Yao bring ivory and slaves from its shores to the coast.

lakes.name: Lake Tanganyika
lakes.about: A long lake deep in Africa, unknown to Europeans; the people of Ujiji fish it.

lakes.name: Lake Nalubaale
lakes.about: The great lake of the Ganda, whose kabaka rules its north-western shore; nobody outside Africa knows that the Nile flows out of it.

lakes.name: Sea of Aral
lakes.about: The Sea of Aral, the Sea of Islands, where the Jaxartes and the Oxus end in the desert; the Karakalpaks fish it.

lakes.name: Lake Okeechobee
lakes.about: The great lake of the Florida peninsula, of the Seminoles, which Spain has never mapped.

lakes.name: Lake of Nicaragua
lakes.about: The Lake of Nicaragua, fresh water with sharks in it, which reaches the Caribbean by the San Juan; the Spanish town of Granada stands on it.

lakes.name: Lake Chad
lakes.about: A great lake in the middle of Africa, at the heart of the empire of Bornu.

lakes.name: Lake Wener
lakes.about: Lake Wener, the greatest of Sweden's lakes, between Wermeland and West Gothland; its iron goes out by the Gotha to Gothenburg.

lakes.name: Lake Onega
lakes.about: Lake Onega, in Olonets, where the Empress's foundries cast cannon at Petrozavodsk.

lakes.name: Lake Tzana
lakes.about: Lake Tzana of Abyssinia, through which the Abay passes; the emperors' city of Gondar stands north of it.

lakes.name: Lake of Titicaca
lakes.about: Titicaca, the high lake of the Incas, where they said the sun was born; Tupac Catari's rebels came from its country to besiege La Paz in 1781.

lakes.name: Kati Thanda
lakes.about: A great salt lake of the interior of New Holland, often dry, which no European knows.

lakes.name: Great Salt Lake
lakes.about: A salt lake of the far interior, which the Spanish fathers Domínguez and Escalante heard of from the Utes in 1776 and never saw.

lakes.name: Lagoa Mirim
lakes.about: A lagoon on the disputed border between Spain's lands and Portugal's, below Rio Grande.

lakes.name: Wollaston Lake
lakes.about: A lake of the northern forest, of the Chipewyan, which sends its water two ways at once.

lakes.name: Reindeer Lake
lakes.about: A long lake of rock and spruce in the Chipewyan country, north of the Churchill.

lakes.name: Lake of the Woods
lakes.about: The Lake of the Woods, which the peace of 1783 made a corner of the boundary between the British and the United States, by a map that is wrong.

lakes.name: Lake Nipigon
lakes.about: Lake Nipigon, north of Lake Superior, where the French kept a post among the Ojibwe.

lakes.name: Lake Manitoba
lakes.about: Lake Manitoba, named for the spirit the Cree hear in its narrows.

lakes.name: Lake Winnipegosis
lakes.about: The Little Winnipeg, west of the great lake, on the canoe road to the Saskatchewan.

lakes.name: Lake of the Hills
lakes.about: The Lake of the Hills, where the North West Company built Fort Chipewyan in 1788, the furthest post of the fur trade, from which Mackenzie set out.

lakes.name: Lake Mistassini
lakes.about: A great lake of the Cree in the interior of Labrador, which a French Jesuit reached in 1672.

lakes.name: Georgian Bay
lakes.about: The great eastern bay of Lake Huron, the end of the canoe road from the Ottawa River to the west.

lakes.name: Lake Saimaa
lakes.about: The lakes of Saimaa in Swedish Finland, so many and so linked that a boat can go a hundred miles among them; the Russian border has run through them since 1743, and the war is fought along them now.

lakes.name: Lake Maeler
lakes.about: Lake Maeler, the long lake behind Stockholm, of a thousand islands, whose water reaches the sea through the city.

lakes.name: Laguna Madre
lakes.about: A long lagoon behind the sandbars of the coast of New Santander.

lakes.name: Zuyder Zee
lakes.about: The Zuyder Zee, the South Sea of the Dutch, which the sea broke into in the Middle Ages; Amsterdam's ships come in by it past the shoals of the Pampus.

lakes.name: Putrid Sea
lakes.about: The Putrid Sea, the shallow, stinking lagoons behind the Arabat spit, where the Crimea joins the mainland; the salt of Perekop is gathered on it.

lakes.name: Issyk-Kul
lakes.about: The warm lake of the Kirghiz, which never freezes, high in the Tien Shan.

lakes.name: Lake of Geneva
lakes.about: The Lake of Geneva, between the Republic of Geneva, the Bernese Pays de Vaud and Savoy; Voltaire lived by it.

lakes.name: Lake Wetter
lakes.about: Lake Wetter, clear and cold, in the middle of Sweden; Jönköping stands at its southern end.

lakes.name: Lake Ilmen
lakes.about: Lake Ilmen, at whose outlet stands Novgorod the Great, the old mother of Russian cities.

lakes.name: Lake Peipus
lakes.about: Lake Peipus, on whose ice Alexander Nevsky beat the Teutonic Knights in 1242.

lakes.name: Dead Sea
lakes.about: The Dead Sea, the Asphaltites, so salt that nothing lives in it and a man floats.

lakes.name: Lake Champlain
lakes.about: Lake Champlain, the war road between New York and Canada, with Ticonderoga at its southern end.

lakes.name: Lough Neagh
lakes.about: Lough Neagh, the largest lake in the British Isles, famous for its eels.

lakes.name: Lake of Van
lakes.about: The Lake of Van, salt and bitter, in Turkish Armenia.

lakes.name: Lake Urmia
lakes.about: The lake of Urmia in Persian Azerbaijan, too salt for fish.

lakes.name: Koko Nor
lakes.about: Koko Nor, the Blue Lake of the Mongols, where the Manchu Emperor's officers meet the Tibetans.

lakes.name: Frische Haff
lakes.about: The Frische Haff, the lagoon behind the long sand spit, across which Königsberg's trade reaches the sea at Pillau.

lakes.name: Lake Kossogol
lakes.about: Lake Kossogol of the Mongols, deep and clear, which pours into the Selenga.

lakes.name: Lake Enare
lakes.about: Lake Enare, the lake of the Lapps in the far north of Swedish Finland.

lakes.name: Lake Ubsa
lakes.about: A salt lake on the steppe of the Mongols' far north-west.

lakes.name: Tengri Nor
lakes.about: The Heavenly Lake of Tibet, holy to the Tibetans, north of Lhasa.

lakes.name: Dalai Nor
lakes.about: The Sea Lake of the Barga Mongols, on the Manchu Emperor's Russian frontier.

lakes.name: Lake Hinka
lakes.about: Lake Hinka, in the Manchu wilderness east of the Ussuri.

lakes.name: Lake Zaysan
lakes.about: Lake Zaysan, through which the Irtish runs out of the Manchu Emperor's Zungaria toward the Russian line.

lakes.name: Rutanzige
lakes.about: A lake of the Nile's heads, in the hills of Bunyoro and Nkore.

lakes.name: Lake Kivu
lakes.about: A lake at the western edge of the kingdom of Rwanda, among volcanoes.

lakes.name: Lake Tai
lakes.about: Lake Tai, in the richest country of China, ringed by the silk towns of Suzhou and Wuxi.

lakes.name: Lake Poyang
lakes.about: Poyang Lake, the largest in China, which the Kiang fills in summer; the porcelain of Jingdezhen goes out across it.

lakes.name: Lake Taupo
lakes.about: The great lake in the middle of New Zealand's northern island, of the Tūwharetoa, unknown to Europeans.

seas.name: Frozen Ocean
seas.about: The Frozen Ocean, whose ice turned back Cook's ships in 1778, and every seeker of a passage to the north-west or the north-east before him.

seas.name: Southern Ocean
seas.about: The ocean of the far south, where Cook, the first to cross the Antarctic circle, sailed round the world in 1773 and 1774 and found ice, not a continent.

seas.name: Atlantic Ocean
seas.about: The Western Ocean, crossed every year by fleets of merchantmen, slavers and sugar ships: the highway of Europe's empires.

seas.name: Pacific Ocean
seas.about: The South Sea of the Spaniards, which Cook crossed three times and where the Manila galleon still sails once a year to Acapulco.

seas.name: Indian Ocean
seas.about: The ocean of the monsoons, which the East India ships cross to Madras, Bombay and Canton, and the dhows from Muscat to Zanzibar.

seas.name: Black Sea
seas.about: The Euxine, which the Turks kept closed to all ships but their own for three hundred years; the Russians have built a fleet at Sebastopol since 1783.

seas.name: Philippine Sea
seas.about: The sea east of the Philippines, which the Manila galleon crosses outward bound.

seas.name: Tasman Sea
seas.about: The sea between New Holland and New Zealand, which Tasman crossed in 1642; the ships of the new colony at Sydney Cove sail it.

seas.name: Bay of Bengal
seas.about: The Bay of Bengal, which the Company's ships cross to Madras and Calcutta; the storms of the monsoon are its terror.

seas.name: China Sea
seas.about: The China Sea of the Company's ships, crossed with the monsoon on the way to Canton.

seas.name: Arabian Sea
seas.about: The sea between Arabia and India, of the dhows of Muscat and the Company's ships to Bombay.

seas.name: Beaufort Sea
seas.about: The sea of ice off the northern coast of America, which no ship has sailed; Mackenzie saw its ice at the mouth of his river last summer.

seas.name: Caribbean Sea
seas.about: The sea of the sugar islands, of Jamaica, Saint-Domingue and Havana, where the empires of Europe have fought for two hundred years.

seas.name: Gulf of Mexico
seas.about: Spain's sea, ringed by her coasts from Florida to Yucatan; the treasure fleets once gathered at Havana for home.

seas.name: Labrador Sea
seas.about: The sea between Labrador and Greenland; the Moravian brethren keep missions on the Labrador coast.

seas.name: Hudson's Bay
seas.about: The Company's bay, where the Hudson's Bay Company's ships come once a year to York Factory and Churchill for the furs.

seas.name: Caspian Sea
seas.about: The Caspian, the great salt lake of the world, where the Russians of Astrakhan trade with Persia.

seas.name: Baffin's Bay
seas.about: Baffin's Bay, which William Baffin sailed in 1616; whalers go there and nobody else.

seas.name: Gulf of Alaska
seas.about: The gulf where the Russians hunt sea otters from Kodiak, and the Spanish have lately come north to claim the coast.

seas.name: Red Sea
seas.about: The Red Sea, the coffee road from Mocha to Jedda; the Porte forbids Christian ships to sail on north to Suez.

seas.name: Sea of Ochotsk
seas.about: The sea at the end of Siberia, which the Russians sail from Okhotsk to Kamtschatka.

seas.name: Weddell Sea
seas.about: An icy sea of the far south, which no ship has entered.

seas.name: Persian Gulf
seas.about: The Gulf of Persia, of pearls and of the Company's factory at Bussorah.

seas.name: Mediterranean Sea
seas.about: The Middle Sea, where the corsairs of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli take the ships of every nation that has not paid them.

seas.name: Ross Sea
seas.about: An icy sea of the far south, which no ship has entered.

seas.name: Coral Sea
seas.about: The sea of the reefs, where Cook's Endeavour struck the reef in 1770 and nearly sank.

seas.name: Sea of Japan
seas.about: The sea between Japan and Corea, which La Pérouse sailed in 1787, the first European to map it.

seas.name: Celebes Sea
seas.about: The sea of the Sulu raiders, who take captives from every island round it.

seas.name: Sulu Sea
seas.about: The sea of the Sultan of Sulu, whose raiders and pearl divers sail it.

seas.name: Norwegian Sea
seas.about: The sea off the coast of Norway, of the cod fisheries of the Lofoten.

seas.name: Greenland Sea
seas.about: The sea of the whalers, where English and Dutch ships hunt in the ice off Greenland.

seas.name: Banda Sea
seas.about: The sea of the Spice Islands, where the Dutch Company guards the nutmeg of Banda.

seas.name: Luzon Strait
seas.about: The strait between Formosa and Luzon, where the typhoons come through.

seas.name: Bay of Biscay
seas.about: The Bay of Biscay, feared by every sailor for its storms.

seas.name: Mozambique Channel
seas.about: The channel between Africa and Madagascar, which the Portuguese watch from the island of Mozambique.

seas.name: Gulf of Guinea
seas.about: The Gulf of Guinea, the coast of the slave trade, from the forts of the Gold Coast to the Bight of Benin.

seas.name: Baltic Sea
seas.about: The Baltic, the East Sea of the Swedes, where Sweden and Russia have been at war since 1788.

seas.name: Barents Sea
seas.about: The sea off Lapland and Novaya Zemlya, where the Pomors hunt walrus and the Dutch once looked for a way to China.

seas.name: German Ocean
seas.about: The German Ocean, the herring sea of the Dutch, between Britain and the Continent.

seas.name: Irish Sea
seas.about: The sea between Britain and Ireland, crossed every day by the packets between Holyhead and Dublin.

seas.name: Java Sea
seas.about: The sea of the Dutch Company's Batavia.

seas.name: Andaman Sea
seas.about: The sea off Pegu and Siam, with the Andaman islands, where the Company has lately planted a settlement.

seas.name: Yellow Sea
seas.about: The sea between China and Corea, yellow with the silt of the Hoang-ho.

seas.name: East China Sea
seas.about: The sea between China, the Loo-Choo islands and Japan, which the Dutch ship from Batavia crosses to Nagasaki.

seas.name: Chukchi Sea
seas.about: The sea beyond Bering's strait, where Cook was turned back by the ice in 1778.

seas.name: Bay of Campeachy
seas.about: The Bay of Campeachy, where English logwood cutters worked until Spain drove them out.

seas.name: Arafura Sea
seas.about: The sea between New Guinea and New Holland, which the men of Macassar cross to gather trepang.

seas.name: Timor Sea
seas.about: The sea south of Timor, which Bligh crossed in an open boat last year after the mutiny on the Bounty.

seas.name: Gulf of Siam
seas.about: The Gulf of Siam, whose new king has ruled from Bangkok since 1782.

seas.name: Laccadive Sea
seas.about: The sea off Malabar and Ceylon, of the pepper coast and the Laccadive islands.

seas.name: Bellingshausen Sea
seas.about: An icy sea of the far south, which Cook skirted in 1774.

seas.name: Amundsen Sea
seas.about: An icy sea of the far south, where Cook reached his farthest south in 1774 and turned back at the ice.

seas.name: Davis's Straits
seas.about: Davis's Straits, which John Davis sailed in 1587 looking for the passage to the north-west; the whalers go there now.

seas.name: Kara Sea
seas.about: The sea of ice beyond Novaya Zemlya, which the Russians have tried and failed to sail through.

seas.name: Laptev Sea
seas.about: The sea off the mouths of the Lena, whose coast the Russians charted in the great northern expedition of the 1730s.

seas.name: Sea of Kamtschatka
seas.about: The sea of Kamtschatka, which Bering sailed in 1728 and 1741, and where he died; the Russian fur hunters cross it to the Aleutians.

seas.name: Sargasso Sea
seas.about: The sea of weed in the middle of the Western Ocean, which Columbus's sailors feared would hold their ships.

seas.name: Great Australian Bight
seas.about: The long southern coast of New Holland, which Pieter Nuyts sailed along in 1627.

seas.name: Gulf of Aden
seas.about: The gulf at the mouth of the Red Sea, past Aden to the straits of Babelmandel.

seas.name: Gulf of Ormus
seas.about: The Gulf of Ormus, at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, where Muscat's ships and the Company's pass.

seas.name: Tuscan Sea
seas.about: The Tuscan Sea, between Italy, Corsica and Sardinia, of Naples and Leghorn.

seas.name: White Sea
seas.about: The White Sea of Archangel, frozen half the year, where the English came to trade with Muscovy in 1553.

seas.name: James Bay
seas.about: The southern end of Hudson's Bay, where the Company keeps Moose Factory and Albany.

seas.name: Gulf of Carpentaria
seas.about: The gulf of northern New Holland, named by the Dutch for their governor Carpentier.

seas.name: Gulf of California
seas.about: The Sea of Cortés, between Spanish Sonora and the peninsula of California, where the Jesuits had their missions.

seas.name: Hudson's Straits
seas.about: The strait into Hudson's Bay, which the Company's ships must pass through the ice every summer.

seas.name: English Channel
seas.about: The Channel, the narrow seas between England and France, which a balloon crossed in 1785.

seas.name: Bay of Honduras
seas.about: The Bay of Honduras, where the British cut logwood and mahogany at Belize by Spain's leave.

seas.name: Gulf of Bothnia
seas.about: The Gulf of Bothnia, between Sweden and Finland, frozen every winter from shore to shore.

seas.name: Gulf of Venice
seas.about: The Gulf of Venice, the Adriatic, which the Republic still calls its own.

seas.name: Gulf of Lyons
seas.about: The Gulf of Lyons, of the mistral, from Marseilles to Spain.

seas.name: Gulf of Florida
seas.about: The Gulf of Florida, the strait through which the Gulf Stream carries the ships home from Havana.

seas.name: Gulf of Tonquin
seas.about: The Gulf of Tonquin, where the Tây Sơn brothers now rule Tonquin.

seas.name: River Plate
seas.about: The River Plate, the wide brown estuary of Buenos Aires and Montevideo; Buenos Aires is the capital of Spain's newest viceroyalty.

seas.name: Straits of Malacca
seas.about: The Straits of Malacca, the gate between the Indian Ocean and the China Sea; the Dutch hold Malacca, and Captain Light founded Pinang for the Company in 1786.

seas.name: Straits of Sincapore
seas.about: The narrow strait at the end of the Malay peninsula, past an island of fishermen and pirates.

seas.name: Straits of Macassar
seas.about: The strait between Borneo and Celebes, of the Bugis traders.

seas.name: Channel of Formosa
seas.about: The channel between China and Formosa, across which the Manchu Emperor sent the army that put down Lin Shuangwen's rising in 1788.

seas.name: Cook's River
seas.about: The inlet Cook went up in 1778, hoping it was a passage, and named a river.

seas.name: Straits of Gibraltar
seas.about: The Straits, held on the north side by the British at Gibraltar, which Spain and France besieged for three years and failed to take.

seas.name: Archipelago
seas.about: The Archipelago, the Aegean of the Greeks, its islands under the Turks; a Russian fleet ruled it in the last war.

seas.name: Gulf of Manaar
seas.about: The Gulf of Manaar, of the pearl fisheries the Dutch of Ceylon farm out.

seas.name: Gulf of Pechelee
seas.about: The Gulf of Pechelee, the sea of Peking.

seas.name: Gulf of Cutch
seas.about: The Gulf of Cutch, of the Rao of Cutch's traders and pirates.

seas.name: Amazon
seas.about: The mouth of the Amazon, so broad that its fresh water can be drunk out of sight of land.

seas.name: Yang-tse-kiang
seas.about: The mouth of the Kiang, its water muddy far out to sea.

seas.name: Oregon
seas.about: The bar of the Oregon, which no ship has yet crossed.

seas.name: Strait of Corea
seas.about: The strait between Corea and Japan, which the Japanese cross to their factory at Fusan.

seas.name: Sea of Azoph
seas.about: The Sea of Azoph, shallow and freezing, which the Russians took from the Turks with the Crimea.

seas.name: Cattegat
seas.about: The Cattegat, between Jutland and Sweden, through which the Baltic trade passes.

seas.name: Gulf of Cambay
seas.about: The Gulf of Cambay, whose tides race in faster than a horse can run.

seas.name: Sea of Candia
seas.about: The Sea of Candia, north of Crete, the Turks' since 1669.

seas.name: Gulf of Genoa
seas.about: The Gulf of Genoa, of the Republic's ships.

seas.name: Delagoa Bay
seas.about: Delagoa Bay, where the Portuguese, the Dutch and the Austrians have each tried a factory.

seas.name: Straits of Magellan
seas.about: The strait Magellan found in 1520, which ships now shun for the open sea round the Horn.

seas.name: Gulf of Oby
seas.about: The long gulf at the mouth of the Oby.

seas.name: Sea of Marmora
seas.about: The Sea of Marmora, between the Dardanelles and Constantinople.

seas.name: Lake of Maracaybo
seas.about: The Lake of Maracaybo, whose villages on piles gave Venezuela its name.

seas.name: Strait of Juan de Fuca
seas.about: The strait the old Greek pilot Juan de Fuca claimed to have found in 1592; Barkley found it again in 1787.

seas.name: Esquimaux Bay
seas.about: A bay of the Labrador coast, where the traders and the Moravians meet the Inuit.

seas.name: Straits of Sangar
seas.about: The strait between Nippon and Jesso, the frontier between the Japanese and the Ainu.

seas.name: Channel of Tartary
seas.about: The channel between Tartary and Saghalien, which La Pérouse sailed in 1787 and thought was closed.

seas.name: Strait of Hainan
seas.about: The strait between the mainland of China and Hainan.

seas.name: Straits of Belle Isle
seas.about: The strait between Newfoundland and Labrador, ice-bound much of the year.

seas.name: Gulf of Darien
seas.about: The Gulf of Darien, where the Scots tried a colony in 1698 and died of fever.

seas.name: The Sound
seas.about: The Sound, where every ship bound for the Baltic pays the King of Denmark's toll at Elsinore.

seas.name: Stettiner Haff
seas.about: The lagoon of the Oder, Stettin's water to the sea at Swinemünde.

seas.name: Frische Haff
seas.about: The Frische Haff, the lagoon behind the long sand spit, across which Königsberg's trade reaches the sea at Pillau.
